# requireState

<link-summary>Asserts that a condition holds, throwing when it does not.</link-summary>

<web-summary>requireState() — Asserts that a condition holds, throwing when it does not. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function requireState(condition: unknown, message?: string): asserts condition;
```

For the checks that are about the moment rather than the arguments: a connection that is already closed, a sheet that has not been prepared yet, a value that was supposed to be cached by now.

It is declared as a TypeScript assertion, so after the call the compiler treats the condition as true for the rest of the function.

## Parameters

| Parameter              | Type      | Description                                                   |
| :--------------------- | :-------- | :------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `condition`            | `unknown` | The condition that must hold.                                 |
| `message` _(optional)_ | `string`  | The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted. |

## Returns

`asserts condition` — nothing; it either passes or throws.

## Throws

| Exception               | Condition               |
| :---------------------- | :---------------------- |
| `IllegalStateException` | the condition is falsy. |

## Examples

### Guarding a state

```javascript
function close(connection) {
  requireState(connection.isOpen, "The connection is already closed.");

  connection.release();
}
```
